title: Enzymatic Assay of Trypsin Inhibition
author: Neilier Junior
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9a4h2gw
materials: Preparation of solutions Trypsin solution: Dilute 1.25 mg of bovine trypsin in 1 mL of water pH 3.0 (adjust with HCl). L-BA p NA stock solution: Dilute 130.47 mg L-BA p NA in 5 mL DMSO (concentration: 6.0 10 -2 M). Store at -20 °C and protected from light. L-BA p NA usage solution (freshly prepared): Dilute 200 mL of stock solution in 10 mL of 100 mM Tris-HCl buffer, pH 8.2 and 20 mM CaCl 2 . Protect from light.

steps.title: Label and prepare microtubes
steps.instruction: Separate three microtubes and label them as “blank”, “control (uninhibited test)”, and “test (inhibited test)”.

steps.title: Add reagents to each tube
steps.instruction: Pipette the following volumes into the labeled tubes:

substeps.instruction: Blank: add 500 µL BA p NA usage solution and 500 µL buffer.
Control: add 100 µL trypsin solution and 400 µL buffer.
Test: add 100 µL enzyme (trypsin), 100 µL leaf extract (source of inhibitors), and 300 µL buffer.

steps.title: Mix, equilibrate, and zero spectrophotometer
steps.instruction: Invert each microtube to mix, then place all three tubes at 25 °C for 5 min. After equilibration, set the spectrophotometer to 410 nm and zero it using the blank tube contents.

steps.title: Start control reaction and record absorbance
steps.instruction: To the control tube add 500 µL BA p NA usage solution, invert to mix, note the exact time, transfer the entire contents to a cuvette, wait 30 s, then monitor absorbance at 410 nm continuously for 120 s.

steps.title: Start test reaction and record absorbance
steps.instruction: To the test tube add 500 µL BA p NA usage solution, invert to mix, note the exact time, transfer the entire contents to a cuvette, wait 30 s, then monitor absorbance at 410 nm continuously for 120 s.

steps.title: Calculate inhibition and inhibitor units
steps.instruction: Using the recorded absorbance data, compute:

substeps.instruction: Percent inhibition = (ΔA₄₁₀ nm control – ΔA₄₁₀ nm test) × 100 / (ΔA₄₁₀ nm control – A₄₁₀ nm blank).
Trypsin inhibitor units per mL = (ΔA₄₁₀ nm control – ΔA₄₁₀ nm test) / (8800 × time × leaf‑extract volume).

Where ΔA₄₁₀ nm control and ΔA₄₁₀ nm test are the absorbance changes in the control and test samples over the 120‑s measurement, A₄₁₀ nm blank is the blank absorbance at 410 nm, 8800 is the extinction coefficient of p‑nitroanilide at 410 nm, time = 120 s, and leaf‑extract volume = 0.1 mL (100 µL).
